\subsubsection{Approach 1: Direct Correlation}

\textbf{Fitting uncertainty}

Parameter estimates: table entries remain approximate local estimate \(\pm\) 95\% confidence intervals from the fitted covariance, parameter standard errors, and residual degrees of freedom.

Plotted uncertainty: shading and error bars show approximate 95\% parameter-uncertainty intervals for fitted or calculated values, conditional on the selected model, preprocessing, and fixed prediction inputs. The app draws 1,000 parameter vectors from the fitted multivariate normal covariance approximation (seed 12345), preserving covariance within each fit; separate fits are sampled independently. Bounds are pointwise 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles, not a simultaneous envelope. Central curves and points use the fitted parameters, not the sampled mean.

No additional residual or observation noise is added. Calibration variability already informs the fitted covariance; the intervals do not include additional scatter of future observations, model-selection uncertainty, or model inadequacy, and are not observation prediction bands. An interval is unavailable if covariance sampling fails or any requested draw is unusable at that point. Unavailable intervals are not zero-width intervals. CV-refit spread is a separate descriptive diagnostic.

\textbf{Prediction uncertainty}

Plotted uncertainty: shading and error bars show approximate 95\% parameter-uncertainty intervals for fitted or calculated values, conditional on the selected model, preprocessing, and fixed prediction inputs. The app draws 1,000 parameter vectors from the fitted multivariate normal covariance approximation (seed 12345), preserving covariance within each fit; separate fits are sampled independently. Bounds are pointwise 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles, not a simultaneous envelope. Central curves and points use the fitted parameters, not the sampled mean.

No additional residual or observation noise is added. Calibration variability already informs the fitted covariance; the intervals do not include additional scatter of future observations, model-selection uncertainty, or model inadequacy, and are not observation prediction bands. An interval is unavailable if covariance sampling fails or any requested draw is unusable at that point. Unavailable intervals are not zero-width intervals. CV-refit spread is a separate descriptive diagnostic.

Time mapping: evaluate the sampled fitted relationship at each fixed supplied in vitro time. Horizontal intervals use the calculated endpoints unchanged, even when they exclude the fitted-parameter point; such intervals are drawn separately rather than shifted. Input and mapped times are checked against the paired-time fitting ranges; points or intervals outside those ranges carry an extrapolation caution.

\subsubsection{Approach 2: Independent Model Fitting}

\textbf{Fitting uncertainty}

Parameter estimates: table entries remain approximate local estimate \(\pm\) 95\% confidence intervals from the fitted covariance, parameter standard errors, and residual degrees of freedom.

Time constants: central tau is evaluated at the fitted parameters by checked numerical integration. Its table standard uncertainty uses 50 draws (seed 12345) and remains unavailable if any sampled tau is invalid. Tau table intervals retain their existing symmetric approximation; plotted time-rescaling intervals instead propagate both parameter vectors directly using the common percentile method below.

Plotted uncertainty: shading and error bars show approximate 95\% parameter-uncertainty intervals for fitted or calculated values, conditional on the selected model, preprocessing, and fixed prediction inputs. The app draws 1,000 parameter vectors from the fitted multivariate normal covariance approximation (seed 12345), preserving covariance within each fit; separate fits are sampled independently. Bounds are pointwise 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles, not a simultaneous envelope. Central curves and points use the fitted parameters, not the sampled mean.

No additional residual or observation noise is added. Calibration variability already informs the fitted covariance; the intervals do not include additional scatter of future observations, model-selection uncertainty, or model inadequacy, and are not observation prediction bands. An interval is unavailable if covariance sampling fails or any requested draw is unusable at that point. Unavailable intervals are not zero-width intervals. CV-refit spread is a separate descriptive diagnostic.

\textbf{Prediction uncertainty}

Plotted uncertainty: shading and error bars show approximate 95\% parameter-uncertainty intervals for fitted or calculated values, conditional on the selected model, preprocessing, and fixed prediction inputs. The app draws 1,000 parameter vectors from the fitted multivariate normal covariance approximation (seed 12345), preserving covariance within each fit; separate fits are sampled independently. Bounds are pointwise 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles, not a simultaneous envelope. Central curves and points use the fitted parameters, not the sampled mean.

No additional residual or observation noise is added. Calibration variability already informs the fitted covariance; the intervals do not include additional scatter of future observations, model-selection uncertainty, or model inadequacy, and are not observation prediction bands. An interval is unavailable if covariance sampling fails or any requested draw is unusable at that point. Unavailable intervals are not zero-width intervals. CV-refit spread is a separate descriptive diagnostic.

Response-value ratio: multiply each sampled in vivo/in vitro curve ratio by the fixed supplied response. The denominator safeguard is unchanged: intervals are withheld when its central 95\% interval includes zero, and exact-zero or nonfinite central denominators make the point unavailable. This is a conservative display safeguard, not a formal ratio-confidence test.

Time-constant ratio: calculate both time constants for each sampled pair of parameter vectors, then multiply their ratio by the fixed prediction time. The original fitted-parameter time scaling remains the center. Failed sampled integrations make the interval unavailable without removing a valid point. This one-scale summary can miss time-dependent differences in curve shape and depends on the extrapolated tail.

Observed-response inverse: invert each sampled in vivo curve at the fixed supplied response, using the same mapping procedure as the central estimate. No response perturbation is added. The common central/sampled mapper starts inside calibration and can extend along a numerically monotonic continuation. It never clips an outside response to an endpoint. Nonunique or numerically flat inverses, nonfinite domains, nonmonotonic continuations, and roots not resolved within the search limit remain unavailable. Calibration-range cautions distinguish extrapolated points from intervals alone extending outside calibration. A finite interval does not establish extrapolation reliability.

Finite intervals that exclude the central estimate are drawn separately at their actual endpoints. Downloads and reports reuse the numerical bounds and include pointwise status and usable-draw counts.

\subsubsection{Approach 3: Direct Mapping}

\textbf{Fitting uncertainty}

Parameter uncertainty: Approach 3 does not fit a parametric model, so there is no fitted-parameter covariance matrix, no parameter confidence intervals, and no model-based 95\% prediction band.

Fitting plots: the plots show interpolation-based ratios/mappings calculated from the preprocessed datasets. They represent deterministic mappings from the supplied data and preprocessing choices, not statistical uncertainty bands.

\textbf{Prediction uncertainty}

Prediction plot error bars: Approach 3 does not generate formal propagated error bars for prediction outputs because no parametric covariance model is fitted.

Uncertainty is therefore limited to the quality of the input data, preprocessing, interpolation, and the assumption that the observed mapping remains valid for the prediction dataset. Lookup ratios outside the interpolation range remain unavailable rather than extrapolated. A supported mapping that produces a time outside observed calibration is flagged.
